notes: εἰ δὲ μή γε taken as one noncompositional cluster on *else* under rule 39, headed on the first particle; splitting *else* across the particles was rejected.
οὐκ carries the clause's single negation as the determiner *no*; no negative indefinite competes, so rules 41 and 59 do not apply.
πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι follows rule 61: the preposition takes the clause-introducer *to*, the nominalizing article is unrepresented, and the infinitive keeps *be seen*.
s026 τῷ governs a verbless prepositional modifier, so under rule 31 it keeps the supplied relativizer *who* while ἐν takes the supplied copula.
